items.mnemonic: At the WATER's edge count TEN waves before the SUN climbs, and TEN more before the MOON pulls them back out. The whole sea breathing in and out — tide.
WATER hurled at a WHITE wall from every DIRECTION, then a STRIKE of the drum for good measure: a storm of spray and noise — intense.
A SMALL BIRD perches too close to the FIRE; its tail feathers curl brown and start to smoke — scorch.
An OLD cook squints at the SUN to check the hour, then feeds the FIRE under the pot until the broth rolls — boil.
Lift the LID: the wide MOUTH of a jar, and inside it a CHILD has hidden a ROUND green plum. Leave it beside the FIRE a few nights and it turns soft and golden — ripen.
CLAW: three curved nails hanging from a hooked paw, ready to snag whatever passes — claw.
A COW wanders off, and the herder gives the fence post a STRIKE with his stick to call her back to the grass — pasture.
A DOG that has crowned itself KING, barking orders at the furniture — crazy.
A DOG and an INSECT share one yard, each pretending the other does not exist — alone.
A DOG wriggles under a bull's HORNS and along its BIG flank to reach the gate; there is barely room to breathe — narrow.
The KING sends a PERSON into the hills for a stone with STREAKS of color no one has ever seen — rare.
One KING lays a SWORD on the floor between himself and a second KING, splitting one court into two teams — squad.
SWEET: a tongue pressing one drop of honey against the roof of the mouth and holding it there — sweet.
A farmer runs FIRE across the stubble, and the ash feeds a dry RICE FIELD on the slope that no water ever reaches — field.
A RICE FIELD mown flat, a COVER of woven straw laid over it, then stacked on a SHELF in neat rectangles — tatami.
Slice a melon into EIGHT with a SWORD and lay every piece on one flat DISH to carry out to the guests — tray.
Watch a DISH BECOME a mountain: rice heaped higher and higher until it spills over the rim — prosper.
A BOAT's crew sets a WEAPON down across a wide DISH, and the flat top becomes the table for their game — board.
An EYE with a STUBBORN stare that refuses to blink first — eyeball.
A HAND shading an EYE as the night nurse scans the ward, checking every bed in turn — watch over.
Rub a HEMP cloth over a STONE, round and round, until it shines like glass — polish.
At the ALTAR a woodcutter sets down his AXE and bows his head — pray.
Among the GRAIN a HEART is buried, marked only by one STROKE scratched on a single stalk — secret.
A sheaf of GRAIN BOUND UP with a SMALL ribbon, a name tag tied to the knot — title.
HOLE: a roof with two legs sticking out beneath it, where someone has dug straight down — hole.
DRAGON: a standing beast with a long tail coiled under its belly, waiting for rain — dragon.
BAMBOO slips a PERSON carries, each notched an INCH from the end so the gatekeeper can match the halves — token.
A BAMBOO pole, a MOON of pale flesh, and POWER: the cord that tightens under the skin when you lift — muscle.
BAMBOO slips in a FRAME on the wall, each pinned to a branch of a TREE drawn in ink: the whole campaign mapped out — plan.
RICE divided into EIGHT, then EIGHT again, under the SWORD until nothing is left but white dust — powder.
A single kernel of RICE made to STAND on its end in the middle of the table — grain.
RICE boiled down in a LEAN-TO, the sticky pot scraped out with a BROOM, and a MOUTH already open for the first taste — sugar.
One STROKE from above catches the THREAD and pulls it taut into a line of ancestors — lineage.
THREAD dyed by a CRAFT so careful the color never fades — crimson.
THREAD so fine it slips through a ring the size of a MOUTH and shines like the MOON — silk.
THREAD braided thick, hung over a FRAME, looped around the HORNS of the shrine gate and run up the MOUNTAIN path for pilgrims to grip — rope.
The RETAINER's RIGHT HAND winds the THREAD tighter and tighter until it hums — tense.
THREAD under a ROOF where a PERSON spends ONE night: by morning the WHITE shirt on the line has pulled in on itself — shrink.
Caught in a NET, made to SAY what you did, then handed a SWORD-sharp fine — punishment.
FEATHERS spread over a RICE FIELD, TWENTY in every row and EIGHT rows deep: a span wide enough to lift a bird — wing.
Drag the PLOW past the WELL and turn the soil over until the rows run straight — till.
MOON-pale flesh stretched smooth over a TABLE, warm to the touch — skin.
A MOON of dark flesh hung on the CLOTHESLINE to dry, heavy and glistening — liver.
Under a LID the MOON of flesh fills like CLOTH billowing on a line, then empties again — lung.
A whole RICE FIELD's harvest ends up in this MOON-shaped pouch of flesh — stomach.
A MOON of flesh under a SPOON left out in the SUN: it slowly melts into grease — fat.
A MOON-pale limb pushes off the EARTH; its PRIVATE strength is in the knee, folded like a SEAL stamp — leg.
The MOON of flesh that turns toward the WEST when a WOMAN twists around to look behind her — waist.
TONGUE: the flap that pokes out of a mouth and tastes a thousand things — tongue.
GRASS clipped so short that the mower's ZIGZAG path still shows across the yard — lawn.
GRASS so high that a HALBERD planted in it disappears to the handle — lush.
GRASS bundled for a PERSON to carry, hooked on a NAIL and balanced on one shoulder, with a MOUTH grumbling at the weight — baggage.
GRASS plucked by a CLAW from the top of a low TREE: leaves for tonight's pot — vegetable.
GRASS in full bloom: TWENTY petals on ONE stalk, TEN stalks in a row, every color at once — splendor.
GRASS laid over the pot, a cloth to FINISH it, WATER beneath, ONE log and a FIRE below: white clouds curl up through the leaves — steam.
GRASS gathered for the UNICORN, the beast said to point its horn only at the worthy — recommend.
A TIGER's skin stretched over a ROW of posts, with nothing at all inside it — empty.
The same BLOOD runs in every PERSON here, and they stand shoulder to shoulder, PERSON after PERSON, filling the square — masses.
GO down the middle, where two squares of EARTH, EARTH stacked like paving stones, mark the way between the shops — street.
GO around the STOCKADE on patrol, lantern raised, all night long — guard.
TEN measured cuts of a HALBERD-sharp blade through the CLOTHES on the tailor's table, each one final — judge.
A BONE-dry seam gives way under the SWORD and the CLOTHES tear from collar to hem — split.
A COW-hide sheet, a CLOTH pattern, a SWORD to cut it, and CLOTHES stitched by the hundred on a factory floor — manufacture.
What you SAY and what you BECOME finally match — sincerity.
SAY the news with one long STROKE of the bell, STOP all work, and STRETCH out your arms to welcome the newcomer — birth.
SAY it kindly, offer a sheaf of GRAIN, and throw a LASSO of charm around the guest's shoulders — invite.
SAY a name into the dark and only a SMALL BIRD answers from the fence — who?
SAY it with your whole BODY, bowing an INCH lower each time — apologize.
SAY "after you", lift the LID, let the other MOUTH drink first from the WELL, and even hand over your CLOTHES against the cold — yield.
A MOON of fat on a PIG rolling happily in the mud — pig.
In the MIDDLE of the chest, under ONE lock, the family's finest SHELL coins — precious.
A PERSON hires a PORTER and pays him in SHELL coins at the end of the road — fare.
SHELL coins pushed through the LATTICE of the shop window, and the goods handed back the same way — purchase.
You RUN toward it, EAR first, RIGHT HAND reaching for it before you know why — interest.
A FOOT measures off the floor one GIANT stride at a time — distance.
A FOOT reads the cracks in the ground like an OMEN and springs clear of them — leap.
A FOOT starts tapping, the BEAK-shaped hat nods along, and soon you UTILIZE every limb you own — dance.
A CAR parked under the CLOTHESLINE strung from the roof's edge, right where the rain drips off — eaves.
A CAR on each side, one LID of sky over both, and FATHER walking around them, weighing which to buy — compare.
TEN crates, a HALBERD strapped on top, all heaved into the CAR until the axle groans — load.
A RAY of light breaks through the COVER of cloud and every CAR in the lot flashes back at the sky — shine.
SPICY: a needle standing upright on the tongue, the sting that makes your eyes water — spicy.
A ROAD narrows between WHITE cliffs that lean in closer with every step — press.
The ROAD runs through GRAIN so thin you can see the far hills through it, and a LASSO of light passes straight through — transparent.
On the ROAD you meet a MONKEY and must decide how to handle it: feed it, or bow and pass — treat.
Past the LID of smog, FATHER drives out to the quiet TOWN at the edge of the city — suburbs.
One DROP of ink on a STUBBORN brow: a boy from the TOWN signing his name for the first time — son.
